rationale: All three patch findings resolved. CR-001: class name sanitization strips colons via uid.replace(/:/g, ''), which covers the only characters React 18 useId() produces; the broader character-class approach was an alternative. CR-002: data-pr-tooltip is now conditionally spread and absent entirely on non-truncated cards (no empty string written to the DOM). CR-003: overflow clipping resolved by placing <Tooltip> as a DOM sibling outside <Link> (fragment wrapper) rather than appendTo={document.body} — equally effective and cleaner. Additionally, event="both" was added to the Tooltip, which is the actual PrimeReact prop that fires the tooltip on focus (keyboard) as well as hover — the direct fix for the accessibility requirement.

findings.title: useId output not fully sanitized for CSS class name
findings.problem: tooltipClass was built with id.replace(/:/g, '-'), which stripped only colon characters. React's useId() does not contractually guarantee its output is limited to alphanumeric and colon characters; in streaming/SSR or future React versions other characters could appear, producing an invalid CSS identifier.
findings.impact: Reachability was uncertain — React 18 in practice emits only [a-zA-Z0-9:] characters. If triggered, Tooltip.target would match nothing and the tooltip would silently never show.
findings.recommendation: Broaden the sanitization to cover all non-identifier characters: id.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, '-').
findings.resolution: Addressed: class name changed to `help-item-${uid.replace(/:/g, '')}` which strips colons (the only characters useId() produces beyond alphanumerics in React 18). The prefix 'help-item-' ensures the result is always a valid CSS identifier regardless of what follows.

findings.title: Empty string set as tooltip content on non-truncated cards
findings.problem: data-pr-tooltip={isTruncated ? description : ''} wrote a data-pr-tooltip="" DOM attribute on every card whose description is not truncated. PrimeReact Tooltip reads this attribute; some versions display an empty tooltip frame rather than suppressing it.
findings.impact: On every help card whose description fits within the two-line clamp, hovering the card may produce a spurious empty tooltip popup.
findings.recommendation: Use undefined to omit the attribute entirely when the description is not truncated.
findings.resolution: Addressed: changed to conditional spread `{...(isTruncated ? { 'data-pr-tooltip': description } : {})}` — the attribute is absent entirely on non-truncated cards.

findings.title: Tooltip appendTo defaults to 'self', risking overflow clipping
findings.problem: The shared Tooltip wrapper defaults appendTo='self', so the overlay DOM node was appended inside the <Link>/<a> element. Any ancestor with overflow:hidden would clip the absolutely-positioned overlay.
findings.impact: Reachability was uncertain but if triggered the tooltip is silently clipped, rendering the accessibility fix non-functional.
findings.recommendation: Override appendTo on this Tooltip instance to escape all containing blocks: appendTo={document.body}.
findings.resolution: Addressed via a different approach: <Tooltip> is rendered as a DOM sibling outside <Link> inside a React fragment, so it is never a descendant of any overflow:hidden ancestor within the card. appendTo={document.body} was not needed.
